messages:
incident-bot: Page triggered: INC-2026-0850 at 2026-05-11 16:12:45 UTC. Severity: Sev2. Auto-acknowledged by Maria at 16:12:52 UTC. Escalation timer set to 16:27 UTC.

Maria: I’m taking comms. Initial alert shows elevated tail latency and 5xx errors for a subset of AtlasWorks’ Dedicated capacity in eu-central-1. @Devin please take infra lead; @Anshu pull metrics and timeline. I’ll draft the customer follow-up for AtlasWorks once we have mitigations.

Anshu: Quick signals:
- 16:12:10 UTC: request queue depth rose for model-group-2 from ~90 -> ~1200
- 16:12:38 UTC: 5xx rate peaked at 18% for AtlasWorks' routes
- 16:13:05 UTC: autoscaler attempted to add replicas but several pulls returned 504/timeouts from internal registry mirror
- 16:15:40 UTC: routing change to warm pool applied, queue draining begins

Devin: Taking lead. Mitigations in progress: route traffic to warm pool, force-add reserved nodes, and temporarily relax healthcheck grace for replicas to avoid thrashing. Executing commands now.

Devin: Commands used during mitigation:
```
# route AtlasWorks traffic to warm pool in eu-central-1
rctl route set --region eu-central-1 --customer AtlasWorks --target warm-pool

# emergency reserved capacity
rctl capacity add --region eu-central-1 --count 5 --type reserved --reason "INC-2026-0850 emergency"

# relax healthcheck grace period to avoid restart storms
rctl config set --service inference --region eu-central-1 --key healthcheck_grace --value 60s
```

Maria: Thanks. Timeline and mitigation summary look good. Li/Sophie, we need a short customer-facing note plus the statuspage blurb. We must offer AtlasWorks their SLA credit proactively and propose a 1-hour technical review. Sophie can you coordinate the specifics?

Sophie (cs): Will do. Draft customer email below (short):

```
Subject: Follow-up: Service disruption in eu-central-1 (May 11)

Hi AtlasWorks team,

We want to follow up on the service disruption on May 11 between 16:12 and 16:30 UTC that affected your Dedicated capacity in eu-central-1.

What happened: During a scaling event, a subset of nodes experienced image-pull timeouts from an internal mirror registry which delayed autoscaler provisioning and caused elevated latency and transient 5xx errors for some requests.

Impact: Some API requests experienced elevated latency or returned errors during the incident window. No customer data was accessed or exposed.

What we did: We temporarily routed your traffic to our pre-warmed capacity, added reserved nodes, and adjusted healthcheck timing to stabilize replicas. Service returned to normal by 16:30 UTC.

Next steps: We are publishing a post-incident report that includes the full timeline and actions we’re taking (mirror fixes, pull-retry backoffs, and autoscaler gating). As an immediate remediation we will:
- add a redundant registry mirror for eu-central-1
- implement image pre-pull for hot model pools during deploys
- add autoscaler circuit-breaker for repeated image-pull failures

We will offer a prorated SLA credit for the SLO breach and a 1-hour technical review with our infra team. Please reply if you’d like us to process the credit and preferred times for the review.

Apologies for the disruption,
Redwood Inference Support
```

Li: Two small edits: say "internal mirror registry timeouts for a subset of nodes" and mention the exact mitigation timestamps in the email body (warm routing at 16:15:40 UTC, reserved nodes added at 16:16:10 UTC).

Maria: Good catch. Anshu, Devin, please confirm those times so I can lock the email. Also, Jordan prepare statuspage copy with the short resolved update.

Anshu: Confirmed: warm routing applied at 16:15:40 UTC, reserved nodes added at 16:16:10 UTC, normal routing restored at 16:30:05 UTC. Adding these to the internal timeline.

Devin: Will add CLI session logs and autoscaler trace to the postmortem appendix. Noting for runbooks: add runbook step to route to warm pool at queue_depth >= 400 or if image-pull errors > 3% sustained for 30s.

Jordan: Statuspage draft (public):
```
Incident: Elevated 5xx errors and latency in eu-central-1
Detected: 2026-05-11 16:12 UTC
Resolved: 2026-05-11 16:30 UTC
Summary: Image-pull timeouts from an internal mirror registry delayed autoscaler provisioning for a subset of nodes. Traffic was routed to warm capacity and reserved nodes were provisioned. No customer data exposure.
Impact: Some API requests experienced elevated latency or transient 5xx errors for customers in the region.
```

Anshu: Suggest one small accuracy tweak: change "image-pull timeouts from an internal mirror registry" -> "image-pull timeouts observed for a subset of nodes pulling from internal mirror registry (registry throttling)".

Maria: Approved with that wording change and with the postmortem link appended once the report is ready. Sophie, will you be the approver for the final email?

Sophie (cs): Yes I can approve after the small timestamp edits. Also I’ll coordinate offering the SLA credit proactively.

Rachel (finance): For AtlasWorks on Dedicated, the credit will be calculated per contract formula. If you DM the exact incident window and their committed monthly spend I’ll compute the amount and queue payment.

Maria: On-call handoff notes for the postmortem: I acknowledged at 16:12:52 UTC, Devin took lead at 16:13:30 UTC ("taking infra lead - routing to warm pool"), handed back to Maria at 16:20:00 UTC for comms. Please include these lines in the timeline appendix.

Devin: Adding: exact commands executed, autoscaler traces, and the rctl session log to the appendix. Also adding a short remediation task: add pre-pull in eu-central-1 during hot deploys and add retry backoff to image-puller.

Anshu: Also proposing a paging review: our escalation timer was fine but we should consider lowering the auto-route threshold to 400 queue depth for Dedicated customers. Adding to retro action items.

Jordan: I’ll post the statuspage resolved update under @redwood-status at 17:00 UTC after Maria gives final sign-off. Will include link to postmortem PDF when available.

Sophie (cs): Approve the customer email with inserted timestamps. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0850 status updated -> Resolved at 2026-05-11 16:30:05 UTC. Postmortem assigned to Maria, Devin, Anshu.

Maria: Recap / action items:
- Devin / Anshu: finalize postmortem draft with timeline, logs, and runbook changes by EOD tomorrow
- Rachel: compute SLA credit amount and DM Maria
- Sophie / Li: send customer email to AtlasWorks once credit confirmed
- Jordan: publish statuspage resolved update at 17:00 UTC after sign-off, link postmortem when ready
- SRE: add runbook automation to route earlier on image-pull error signals

Maria: Thanks everyone. Closing thread once the email is sent and the statuspage has the postmortem link.
